  kind: conjugation
  form: potential
  name: "Brandon Japanese::Genki II::Lesson 13::Potential Practice"
  deck_id: 1047286103
  model_id: 1607392351
  model_name: "Japanese Pattern"
  description: "Potential-form practice for selected verbs taught or exemplified on Genki II Lesson 13 textbook pages 26–28 and 32."
  output: "brandon-japanese-genki-ii-lesson-13-potential-pr-221074117d.apkg"
  source: ../normalized/vocabulary.json
  form_note: >-
    Potential expresses ability or possibility (“can / be able to”). Potential
    verbs conjugate like ichidan (る) verbs, so the example may change tense,
    polarity, or politeness. With most を-verbs, either が or を is possible;
    できる takes が almost all the time. Other particles stay unchanged.

    - word:まつ:まつ
    - word:およぐ:およぐ
    - word:行く:いく
    - word:しぬ:しぬ
    - word:読む:よむ
    - word:あそぶ:あそぶ
    - word:買う:かう
    - word:見る:みる
    - word:来る:くる
    - word:する:する
    - word:書く:かく
    - word:飼う:かう
    - word:弾く:ひく

  drill_examples:
    "word:話す:はなす":
      - japanese: 私は日本語が話せます。
        furigana: 私[わたし]は 日本語[にほんご]が 話[はな]せます。
        english: I can speak Japanese.
        register: polite
        audio: audio/janki-3daceb701c03.wav
      - japanese: 英語も話せる？
        furigana: 英語[えいご]も 話[はな]せる？
        english: Can you speak English too?
        register: casual
        audio: audio/janki-4871d4ab4a8a.wav
    "word:まつ:まつ":
      - japanese: もう少しここでまてますか。
        furigana: もう 少[すこ]しここでまてますか。
        english: Can you wait here a little longer?
        register: polite
        audio: audio/janki-fd9b0107354f.wav
      - japanese: もう少しここでまてる？
        furigana: もう 少[すこ]しここでまてる？
        english: Can you wait here a little longer?
        register: casual
        audio: audio/janki-3eb6da066130.wav
    "word:およぐ:およぐ":
      - japanese: 私はおよげないんです。
        furigana: 私[わたし]はおよげないんです。
        english: The truth is, I can't swim.
        register: polite
        audio: audio/janki-e3f245fc2780.wav
      - japanese: 海でおよげる？
        furigana: 海[うみ]でおよげる？
        english: Can you swim in the ocean?
        register: casual
        audio: audio/janki-0fc987bc9e9f.wav
    "word:行く:いく":
      - japanese: 雨が降ったので、海に行けませんでした。
        furigana: 雨[あめ]が 降[ふ]ったので、 海[うみ]に 行[い]けませんでした。
        english: We couldn't go to the beach because it rained.
        register: polite
        audio: audio/janki-7e0c0f147499.wav
      - japanese: 明日は私も行けるよ。
        furigana: 明日[あした]は 私[わたし]も 行[い]けるよ。
        english: I can go tomorrow too.
        register: casual
        audio: audio/janki-ddc8831e5dd5.wav
    "word:しぬ:しぬ":
      - japanese: これで安心してしねます。
        furigana: これで 安心[あんしん]してしねます。
        english: Now I can die in peace.
        register: polite
        audio: audio/janki-065329b77ec2.wav
      - japanese: これで安心してしねる。
        furigana: これで 安心[あんしん]してしねる。
        english: Now I can die in peace.
        register: casual
        audio: audio/janki-2440501ca7d7.wav
    "word:読む:よむ":
      - japanese: この漢字が読めますか。
        furigana: この 漢字[かんじ]が 読[よ]めますか。
        english: Can you read this kanji?
        register: polite
        audio: audio/janki-b1e52ad98f7d.wav
      - japanese: この字、読める？
        furigana: この 字[じ]、 読[よ]める？
        english: Can you read this character?
        register: casual
        audio: audio/janki-0623a3ff7465.wav
    "word:あそぶ:あそぶ":
      - japanese: 明日の午後、あそべますか。
        furigana: 明日[あした]の 午後[ごご]、あそべますか。
        english: Can you hang out tomorrow afternoon?
        register: polite
        audio: audio/janki-4d4f24caf38d.wav
      - japanese: 明日は公園であそべるよ。
        furigana: 明日[あした]は 公園[こうえん]であそべるよ。
        english: I can play at the park tomorrow.
        register: casual
        audio: audio/janki-efb7f385e622.wav
    "word:買う:かう":
      - japanese: この店で切符が買えます。
        furigana: この 店[みせ]で 切符[きっぷ]が 買[か]えます。
        english: You can buy tickets at this store.
        register: polite
        audio: audio/janki-cb9b612fb9b5.wav
      - japanese: この店ではおみやげも買えるよ。
        furigana: この 店[みせ]ではおみやげも 買[か]えるよ。
        english: You can buy souvenirs at this store too.
        register: casual
        audio: audio/janki-cac4a37816ed.wav
    "word:見る:みる":
      - japanese: この動物園ではパンダが見られます。
        furigana: この 動物園[どうぶつえん]ではパンダが 見[み]られます。

        audio: audio/janki-a6e59debedfc.wav

        furigana: この 映画[えいが]は 家[いえ]でも 見[み]られるよ。
        english: You can watch this movie at home too.
        register: casual
        audio: audio/janki-2f2f19feae82.wav
    "word:来る:くる":
      - japanese: 土曜日に来られますか。
        furigana: 土曜日[どようび]に 来[こ]られますか。
        english: Can you come on Saturday?

        audio: audio/janki-8608767fc949.wav
      - japanese: 明日のパーティーに来られる？
        furigana: 明日[あした]のパーティーに 来[こ]られる？
        english: Can you come to tomorrow's party?
        register: casual
        audio: audio/janki-2862251a570f.wav
    "word:する:する":

        furigana: 何[なに]か 楽器[がっき]ができますか。
        english: Can you play any instruments?

        audio: audio/janki-8864d96b98aa.wav
    "word:弾く:ひく":

        audio: audio/janki-4a7ed50f36ee.wav
    "word:吹く:ふく":

## Audience

Default material targets a beginner or lower-intermediate learner following a
Genki-style sequence.

## Required fields

Every vocabulary note should have:

- `expression`;
- `reading` when the expression contains kanji;
- at least one concise English meaning;
- a stable `id`.

## Preferred enrichments

- Anki-formatted furigana: a space before every ruby group, punctuation
  included — `今[いま]、 東京[とうきょう]`, never `今[いま]、東京[とうきょう]`,
  because Anki takes everything since the last space as the base and would
  draw the reading over the comma too.
- Hepburn romaji.
- Part of speech.
- Verb group for verbs.
- Transitivity when meaningful.
- Common conjugations for verbs.
- Usage or nuance notes only when they teach something useful.

## English meanings

Use compact dictionary-style meanings on cards:

```yaml
meanings:
  - "to speak"
  - "to talk"
```

Avoid long paragraphs in the meaning field. Put nuance and restrictions under
`usage_notes`.

## Example sentences

Prefer familiar, concrete content. Useful recurring contexts include software
development, electronic music, family, hiking, travel in Japan, restaurants, and
everyday conversation.

A good example:

```yaml
japanese: "毎日、妻と日本語で話します。"
english: "I speak Japanese with my wife every day."
```

Avoid introducing several unknown grammar points merely to demonstrate one word.

## Verb conjugations

Useful starter forms are:

- dictionary/plain affirmative;
- plain negative;
- plain past;
- plain past negative;
- `て`-form;
- potential;
- passive when common or pedagogically relevant.

Do not manufacture forms for words whose analysis is uncertain.

## Furigana and readings

Use the reading that applies in the exact word, not an exhaustive list of every
possible on'yomi and kun'yomi. Kanji-reference decks can store broader reading
information separately.

## Tags

Use lowercase, stable tags where possible:

```text
shirabe verb godan genki::week11 topic::conversation
```

The builder converts whitespace in individual tags to underscores.

# Japanese Content Style Guide

## Audience

Default material targets a beginner or lower-intermediate learner following a
Genki-style sequence.

## Required fields

Every vocabulary note should have:

- `expression`;
- `reading` when the expression contains kanji;
- at least one concise English meaning;
- a stable `id`.

## Preferred enrichments

- Anki-formatted furigana: a space before every ruby group, punctuation
  included — `今[いま]、 東京[とうきょう]`, never `今[いま]、東京[とうきょう]`,
  because Anki takes everything since the last space as the base and would
  draw the reading over the comma too.
- Hepburn romaji.
- Part of speech.
- Verb group for verbs.
- Transitivity when meaningful.
- Common conjugations for verbs.
- Usage or nuance notes only when they teach something useful.

## English meanings

Use compact dictionary-style meanings on cards:

```yaml
meanings:
  - "to speak"
  - "to talk"
```

Avoid long paragraphs in the meaning field. Put nuance and restrictions under
`usage_notes`.

## Example sentences

Prefer familiar, concrete content. Useful recurring contexts include software
development, electronic music, family, hiking, travel in Japan, restaurants, and
everyday conversation.

A good example:

```yaml
japanese: "毎日、妻と日本語で話します。"
english: "I speak Japanese with my wife every day."
```

Avoid introducing several unknown grammar points merely to demonstrate one word.

## Verb conjugations

Useful starter forms are:

- dictionary/plain affirmative;
- plain negative;
- plain past;
- plain past negative;
- `て`-form;
- potential;
- passive when common or pedagogically relevant.

Do not manufacture forms for words whose analysis is uncertain.

## Furigana and readings

Use the reading that applies in the exact word, not an exhaustive list of every
possible on'yomi and kun'yomi. Kanji-reference decks can store broader reading
information separately.

## Tags

Use lowercase, stable tags where possible:

```text
shirabe verb godan genki::week11 topic::conversation
```

The builder converts whitespace in individual tags to underscores.
